title: Dietary Inclusion of Fermented Apple Pomace at 15% Improves Growth and Lactation Performance in Dairy Goats: A Dose-Response Study with Complementary Rat Evidence for a Gut Microbiota–Butyrate–Nrf2/NF-κB Axis
content: Apple pomace, a byproduct of juice processing, poses valorization challenges in circular agriculture. Solid-state fermentation can improve its nutritional quality, but the optimal inclusion level of fermented apple pomace (FAP) in ruminant diets and the underlying systemic mechanisms remain unclear. This study employed a dual-model strategy with five FAP supplementation levels (0–20%). In lactating dairy goats, we determined dietary nutrient composition, lactation performance, rumen fermentation parameters, and serum metabolic and endocrine indices. In rats, we determined hepatic Nrf2/NF-κB signaling, cecal microbiota composition, and short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) concentrations. In goats, the 15% FAP diet achieved the most favorable dietary nutrient composition and nitrogen utilization within the tested range, markedly increased milk yield and average daily gain, reduced the feed-to-milk ratio and somatic cell count, and was accompanied by elevated growth hormone and reduced insulin concentrations, consistent with improved insulin sensitivity. Pooled rumen fluid analysis suggested a descriptive trend toward increased propionate proportion; however, statistical confirmation was not possible because individual VFA proportions were obtained from pooled samples without replication. In rats, 15% FAP was associated with hepatic Nrf2 nuclear translocation and downstream antioxidant activation, suppression of TLR4/NF-κB and pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β), while IL-6 showed a tissue-reparative pattern. These effects were accompanied by enrichment of butyrate-producing genera and elevated cecal butyrate, which was positively correlated with Nrf2 activation and antioxidant capacity and negatively correlated with oxidative damage. All beneficial effects were attenuated at the 20% inclusion level. Collectively, 15% FAP represents the optimal inclusion level within the tested range. The rat mechanistic data suggest a potential gut–butyrate–Nrf2/NF-κB–associated antioxidant/anti-inflammatory axis; however, because these data are correlative and were obtained in a rodent model, this axis should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and requires direct validation in ruminants. The goat production benefits were accompanied by a descriptive trend toward propionate-type rumen fermentation and endocrine remodeling.
